note: From an OpenStreetMap export (tools/osm-to-kit.mjs, 8 October 2026): the platform lengths, the subway at the south end with steps up to each platform, and the platform-level building on the east side. Side platforms stand 2.1 m outside the slow lines, the real tracks 1.25 times real across. Positive v is east. Photos (geograph 3347292 JThomas 2013, 1349953, 1349962 and 1349966 Gerald England 2009, 5557374 and 5797669 England 2017-18, 6372495 Bill Boaden 2020, 6866047 England 2021; Commons 'Levenshulme railway station (8)' and '(12)'): the line is on a brick embankment over the road at the south end; the way in is a two-storey brick block at street level on the east side by the bridge, with stairs up inside (moved here from the west, where the earlier draft had it); on the east platform a long flat-roofed brick building and, just north of it, a barrel-roofed shelter with Northern-blue lower panels, and a second like it towards the south end of the west platform (only seen at the edge of 6866047 and 4005128, so its size is a guess). The real station has no canopy: the canopy is the game's. The car park is on the east side off Station View, between the station and Stockport Road (Levenshulme Market uses it at weekends), drawn about 60 by 25 m, a rough size from the photos. The embankment's arched recesses below the platform building wait for the terrain. Departure boards on each platform and by the booking office; Sheffield stands and the taxi rank on the forecourt by the entrance, placed by eye.
